title: Fixed-point tensor network for compactified boson conformal field theory
authors: Gong Cheng, Dong-Yu Bao, Zheng-Cheng Gu
abstract: Fixed-point (FP) tensor networks provide a discrete spacetime representation of conformal field theories (CFTs), offering a new route toward understanding holographic duality, generalized symmetries, and even quantum gravity. In this work, we construct FP tensors for the 2D compactified boson theory at a generic compactification radius, an archetypal irrational CFT, using boundary (open-string) data with conformal boundary conditions. We show that the resulting tensors reproduce the closed-string spectrum with high accuracy and generate stable renormalization-group (RG) flows under the tensor complex renormalization algorithm. Moreover, we identify a controllable exactly marginal deformation at the level of a single tensor, enabling flows that move continuously along the $c=1$ moduli space. This framework establishes a concrete lattice-level route toward describing a broad class of 2D irrational CFTs.
summary: This work develops a novel fixed-point tensor network approach to describe irrational Conformal Field Theories, using the compactified boson model as a test case. By constructing tensors from boundary data and analyzing them via Tensor Complex Renormalization, the authors successfully reproduce known physical spectra and map out continuous flow paths in the theory's moduli space.
main_problem: The primary goal is extending fixed-point tensor network constructions from rational CFTs to irrational theories, specifically using the 2D compactified boson model.
main_result: The framework successfully generates a discrete lattice description for the irrational CFT, accurately reproducing the closed-string spectrum and identifying controllable exactly marginal deformations along the c=1 moduli space.
method: The authors employ Fixed-Point (FP) tensor networks, utilizing boundary data to construct tensors that are then analyzed using the Tensor Complex Renormalization (TCR) algorithm for RG flow analysis.
model_or_system: The system studied is the 2D compactified boson conformal field theory, which serves as an archetypal irrational CFT. The construction relies on mapping correlation functions onto tensor network contractions involving boundary conditions.
key_observables: Closed-string spectrum (conformal dimensions $\Delta$), central charge ($c$), and scaling dimensions ($\Delta$) extracted via RG flow analysis.
important_parameters: The compactification radius $R$, the deformation parameter $	au$ or $r$, and the finite grid size $\Lambda$ used for numerical approximation.
main_assumptions: The method requires replacing continuous boundary conditions with a finite, discretized lattice representation, which introduces necessary approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the construction of rank-3 and rank-4 FP tensors, show the recovered closed-string spectrum via transfer matrix methods at various radii, and depict RG spectra derived from these tensor structures.
paper_structure: The paper systematically builds the tensor network representation for correlation functions (rank-4 tensors), applies the TCR algorithm to analyze the resulting spectrum, and demonstrates how tuning parameters within the tensor structure generates continuous marginal deformations along moduli spaces.
why_interesting: While focused on CFT, the core methodology—using tensor networks (TCR) to simulate complex quantum field theory dynamics and RG flows—is a powerful numerical technique applicable to strongly correlated systems or open quantum systems where exact diagonalization is impossible.
